title: Materials and Their Uses
seo_title: Grade 3 Science: Materials and Their Uses Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Objects are made of materials such as wood, plastic, metal, glass, paper and cloth. Materials have properties (hard or soft, rough or smooth, bendable, waterproof, transparent) that make them useful. Materials can be reduced, reused and recycled. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 3, Quarter 1: Materials)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 1: Materials): objects and materials, properties of materials, choosing materials and reduce, reuse, recycle. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Each material is chosen for its properties.
body_html:
How to think about it

An object is a thing; a material is what it is made of. A spoon can be made of metal, plastic or wood. Materials have properties: glass is transparent, rubber is bendable, metal is hard and shiny, and plastic is waterproof.

We choose materials for their properties: a raincoat must be waterproof, a window must be transparent, and a cooking pot must not melt. We can help the Earth by reducing waste, reusing bottles and recycling paper and cans.

Example

Why is a window made of glass?

You can see through it.

Answer: glass is transparent

Example

Which material is best for a raincoat?

Water must not pass through.

Answer: plastic or rubber

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up the object and the material.
  • Thinking all metals float.
  • Thinking reusing and recycling are the same.
